roadmap.goal: Fix ADO Bug 5586 — ForecastBase.GetLikelihood(int) reports confidence the simulation does not support, in two independent ways. Defect 1: trialCounter == 0 falls to `return 100`, so an absence of evidence reads as certainty. Defect 2 (confirmed by execution, not by reading): the loop adds a bucket's mass BEFORE testing the break, so GetLikelihood(t) returns CDF(min{k in keys : k >= t}) rather than CDF(t) — correct only when t is itself a bucket key or t > maxKey. Sparse histograms (every AggregatedWhenForecast and every DeliveryCompletionForecast, because CompletionHistogram.DistributeByLargestRemainder emits only days with trials > 0) against an arbitrary working-day target make that error unbounded: {5:5000,40:5000} at day 6 returns 100 where 50 is the truth. The fix expresses the threshold through the injected IComparer rather than a literal `key <= t`, because HowManyForecast passes a DESCENDING comparer over an item-count key and a literal would silently invert it. Acceptance: the new non-key WhenForecast cases and the HowManyForecast at-least-N pin pass; the two existing tests that assert the defect are flipped to the honest expectation and pass; the whole backend suite stays green; the manual When-forecast reports 'cannot forecast' rather than a fabricated 100 % or an equally false 0 %; Stryker per-feature kill rate >= 80 % on the touched scope, with the Delivery.cs guard-3 mutant now dying without a new test.

The RCA is the design doc: it carries the exact corrected method body, the per-subclass comparer analysis that constrains the fix's FORM, the complete file list, and an executed inventory of which existing tests stay green and which two assert the defect. Three steps rather than the two-step bugfix default because the maintainer ruled the manual-forecast surface must report 'cannot forecast' (nullable carrier, ADR-112 precedent) rather than fall to 0 — that is a DTO contract change with its own RED and its own frontend surface, and folding it into the GREEN step would mix a wire-format change into a domain fix. All test edits live in 01-01 so the RED is honest; all production code lives in 01-02 and 01-03.

(c) Add ONE new test for HowManyForecast likelihood pinning at-least-N semantics — HowManyForecast passes a DESCENDING comparer (HowManyForecast.cs:7,12) and its key is an item COUNT, so with {3:10,5:20,8:70} the honest GetLikelihood(5) is 90 ('90 % chance of at least 5 items'). This test is the guard against a future 'simplification' to a literal key <= t; without it root cause C stays open. If HowManyForecast has no existing test class, create one following the WhenForecastTest layout. (d) Flip the two existing tests that assert the defect: AggregatedWhenForecastTest.cs:204 `Assert.That(aggregate.GetLikelihood(0), Is.EqualTo(100))` in EveryContributorWithoutTrials_KeepsTheContributorHistogram becomes Is.Zero — leave the percentile half at :199-202 completely untouched, that invariant is legitimate and is the actual subject of the test; and ForecastServiceTest.cs:162-172 When_FixedThroughput_TargetDateToday_ReturnLikelihood, whose minKey is 13 so 35 items cannot finish in zero days — rename it to say so and assert Is.Zero. steps.name: Express the likelihood threshold through the injected comparer
steps.description: Replace ForecastBase.GetLikelihood (Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/Models/Forecast/ForecastBase.cs:70-95) with the corrected body from the RCA: return 0 when TotalTrials == 0; then walk the SortedDictionary breaking when `keyOrder.Compare(simulation.Key, threshold) > 0` and accumulating AFTER the test rather than before; then the unchanged percentage arithmetic. `var keyOrder = comparer ?? Comparer<int>.Default;` is REQUIRED, not defensive padding — the protected ForecastBase() ctor at :8 leaves the field null and the SortedDictionary at :44 silently falls back to the same default, so a comparer-based loop would NRE without it. Rename the parameter off `daysToTargetDate` (it is an item count for HowManyForecast) — `threshold` or similar; update the three production call sites' argument names only if they use named arguments. Drop the `daysToTargetDate < 0 => return 0` guard: under ascending order the first key is > -1 so the loop breaks immediately and returns 0 anyway (ForecastServiceTest.cs:159 stays green — verified, minKey is 13), and under descending order the guard was actively WRONG ('at least -1 items' is 100 %). Then: delete the four-line `// Stryker disable once all: equivalent while Bug #5586 stands ...` block at Models/Delivery.cs:72-75, keeping the `if (!HasRemainingWork())` guard itself — that guard is now genuinely observable and DeliveryJointForecastTest.cs:96-118 already kills its mutant. Do NOT touch the annotation at Delivery.cs:64-67; it is a different guard and is not #5586-dependent. Finally trim the two comments that become false: Models/Feature.cs:118-119 and Models/Forecast/AggregatedWhenForecast.cs:17-19 both explain that they exist to avoid the trialCounter == 0 branch reporting 100 %. The guards stay; the comments should shrink to a line that says what the code still means (unknown is carried out explicitly, ADR-112) rather than describing a branch that no longer exists — per CLAUDE.md, one line pointing at the ADR, not narration. Same for the XML doc at Tests/Models/FeatureTest.cs:29-34 which claims both branches 'agree by accident'.

steps.name: Manual forecast says 'cannot forecast' instead of a fabricated number
steps.description: ForecastController.RunManualForecastAsync (API/ForecastController.cs:104-107) is the one production caller that was never guarded, so a team with no usable throughput currently ships 100 % and would ship 0 % after 01-02 — both lies. The maintainer ruled for the nullable carrier, matching ADR-112 and Feature.GetLikelhoodForDate's `return null`. RED first: add a controller-level test asserting that a manual forecast for a team whose When-forecast has TotalTrials == 0 leaves Likelihood null, and a frontend test asserting the cannot-forecast rendering. Then: (a) API/DTO/ManualForecastDto.cs:9 `public double Likelihood { get; set; }` -> `public double? Likelihood { get; set; }`; (b) ForecastController.cs:104-107 — only assign when `whenForecast.TotalTrials > 0` alongside the existing `timeToTargetDate > 0`; (c) Lighthouse.Frontend/src/models/Forecasts/ManualForecast.ts — `likelihood: number` -> `likelihood: number | null` on both the interface and the class, and the constructor default from `likelihood = 0` to `likelihood: number | null = null`; (d) Lighthouse.Frontend/src/pages/Teams/Detail/ManualForecaster.tsx:406-420 — the render gate is currently `manualForecastResult.likelihood > 0`, which after 01-02 would ALSO hide a legitimate 0 % (now common, since any target below the histogram's minKey honestly answers 0). Replace it with a null check so a real 0 % renders as 0 % and only null suppresses or shows 'cannot forecast'. Follow whatever the existing cannot-forecast copy is on the delivery surfaces (grep for the string introduced by ADR-112 / US 5587 and reuse it verbatim rather than inventing new wording). Check whether ForecastLikelihood's props type needs to stay non-null — if so, keep the null check at the call site and pass a narrowed number.
